title: introduce-rbacv2-simulator-kms-dryrun-and-audit-proof-bundler
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: Reduce risk when rolling out RBAC v2 policy changes and KMS residency mappings by providing a deterministic dry-run and local simulation path plus an immutable audit artifact bundler. This PR adds three coordinated developer-facing tools: 1) an RBACv2 policy simulator that evaluates policy changes against a configurable set of tenant/operator scenarios (including nested role templates, temporal grants, and operator-scoped exceptions), 2) a KMS dry-run validator which resolves KMS selection heuristics, affinity fallbacks and quota checks without touching production KMS keys, and 3) an Audit Proof Bundler that packages policy change inputs, simulator output, and a signed checksum so infra teams can store verifiable evidence alongside deploys. Summary of changes: new CLI service (rctl simulate) and internal library redwood/security/simulator with a lightweight scenario DSL; kms/dryrun that wire-frames KMS provider selection and upstream compatibility checks; audit/proof-bundler that emits an immutable JSON+sig artifact and S3 uploader with retention metadata. Checklist: [x] unit tests for simulator decision paths, [x] e2e harness against staged policy DB snapshot, [x] docs (console + CLI usage), [x] feature-flag gated (rbac.simulator.enabled=false by default), [x] telemetry events and per-scenario latency histograms. Backwards compatibility: no runtime path changes—simulator and dry-run code paths are read-only by default. Rollout plan: land behind feature flag, opt-in for early enterprise customers via console toggle, run a one-week pilot on redwood-dedicated, iterate based on false-positive/negative policy diffs. Security review: KMS dry-run intentionally prevents key material or credential exchange; it uses cached provider metadata and quota/region heuristics. Audit artifacts are signed with the platform's signing key (rotation-aware) and stored in the immutables bucket; access to artifacts requires org-level RBAC perms. Testing: comprehensive unit coverage added, integration tests run in CI against a mocked KMS cluster and a snapshot of policy-catalog; manual validation performed with three customers in staging. Related work: ties into ENG-4122 (policy rollout safety) and ENG-4231 (tenant residency tooling). Migration notes: operators should run `rctl simulate apply-scan --snapshot <id>` on policy snapshots before large rollouts; artifact bundle IDs are compatible with the Console's policy diff view. CI notes: some flaky integration tests required mocking timeouts; we added retries and a small delay param. Merge: squash merged by Marina Gómez on 2025-09-19. Release notes: Adds RBACv2 policy simulator CLI, KMS dry-run validator, and audit proof bundler to help safely validate cross-tenant policy and KMS changes before rollout.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nice toolset—can the simulator ingest live operator sessions for accuracy? Author: We intentionally kept ingestion to snapshots to avoid PII and to keep runs deterministic; we may add an optional sanitized ingestion later behind a flag.
Marina Gómez: Audit bundles need TTL metadata. Author: Added retention and vault-key annotation to the bundler; docs updated.
Rahul Iyer: Add a warning when dry-run heuristics diverge from live KMS selection. Author: Added a divergence analyzer metric and console warning path when simulator confidence < 0.7.
release_notes: Adds a read-only RBAC v2 policy simulator (CLI + library), a KMS dry-run validator to test provider resolution/affinity without touching keys, and an Audit Proof Bundler that emits signed artifacts for deploy-time evidence. Feature-flag gated; no breaking changes.
